title: Common Gaussian density and derivative envelope
statement:
Let $v>0$ and $M\ge0$, and write $p_v(m,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-m)^2/(2v))$. There is a nonnegative Lebesgue-integrable function $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that for every $m,z\in\mathbb R$ with $|m|\le M$, all three bounds hold:
\[p_v(m,z)\le b(z),\qquad \left|\frac{z-m}{v}p_v(m,z)\right|\le b(z),\qquad \left|\left(\frac{(z-m)^2}{v^2}-\frac1v\right)p_v(m,z)\right|\le b(z).\]
hypotheses_covered: $v$ is a nonzero nonnegative real, hence $v>0$
replaced: For $v>0$ and $M\ge0$, let $p_v(m,z)$ be the Gaussian density with mean $m$ and variance $v$. There exists a nonnegative Lebesgue-integrable $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that $p_v(m,z)\le b(z)$, $|((z-m)/v)p_v(m,z)|\le b(z)$, and $|((z-m)^2/v^2-1/v)p_v(m,z)|\le b(z)$ whenever $|m|\le M$.
